title: A server whose /meta names no version at major 2 is refused locally, and a pin to selvage/1 is not
notes: The rule: a client that can speak `selvage/2`, unpinned, whose `/meta` names no version at major 2 it can speak, MUST NOT connect and MUST NOT fall back to `selvage/1`; the refusal is local, before a socket is opened, and names the version it would need (§2, §10). A pin to a version the server does seat is not that refusal: `selvage/1` is the deliberate choice to host a room the server can read, and a client pinned there joins the link that names `selvage/1`. The two legs differ in the pin alone as far as the rule goes — the first takes a version-2 link, the link a client would speak `selvage/2` on, and the second the version-1 link the pin is for — and the second leg is the positive control: a subject that refuses every link fails it, which is the other way to pass a corpus of refusals. `expectRefusal` asserts the naming and not the sentence, since §2 leaves the words to the client; the version it would need is the one fact both a client of the encrypted wire and a client of the clear one can be held to say. The failure this prevents is the silent downgrade: a compromised or downgraded server advertising one version takes a client that would have spoken the other into a room whose contents that server reads, which is the one failure a confidential wire cannot survive.
